basics.name: Shijie Xiao
basics.label: Ph.D. Student in Computer Science
basics.summary: Ph.D. student in Computer Science at Georgia Tech, co-advised by Prof. Josiah Hester and Prof. Ali Sarhadi. Research focuses on physics-ML hybrid models for weather forecasting, generative AI for probabilistic hazard prediction, and machine learning for behavior analysis.

work.name: Climate Risk & Extreme Dynamics Lab, Georgia Tech (sponsored by Sandia National Laboratories)
work.position: Graduate Research Assistant, advised by Prof. Ali Sarhadi
work.summary: FAST-ML: A Hybrid Physics-Machine Learning Framework for Tropical Cyclone Intensity Forecasting (in preparation for JAMES).
highlights: Developed the FAST-ML framework that embeds neural networks into physics models to build a hybrid physics-ML system.
Engineered differentiable optimization to learn dynamic environmental parameters directly from 3D atmospheric data.
Outperformed the Google state-of-the-art in some cases while preserving physical interpretability.

work.name: Climate Risk & Extreme Dynamics Lab, Georgia Tech
work.position: Graduate Research Assistant, advised by Prof. Ali Sarhadi
work.summary: Physics-based Generative AI for Probabilistic Forecasting of Hurricane-Driven Compound Flooding (in preparation for NMI).
highlights: Built a TensorFlow-based generative emulator that translates tropical cyclone tracks into compound flood fields.
Overcame historical data scarcity by training on massive ensembles of physics-simulated synthetic tracks coupled with complex hydrodynamic and hydraulic simulations.
Slashed computational bottlenecks by generating probabilistic flood maps from ECMWF ensembles in seconds instead of days, enabling real-time, risk-informed emergency planning.

work.name: BrainML Laboratory, Georgia Tech
work.position: Research Intern & Master Thesis, advised by Prof. Anqi Wu
work.summary: A Computational Framework for Multi-Agent Behavior Analysis: Geometric Vision Extraction and Social Attention Inference.
highlights: Conducted research on machine learning methods for trajectory analysis to understand animal behavior patterns.
Implemented algorithms to predict mice movement and modeled spatiotemporal interactions using graph structures.
Developed training pipelines and introduced a novel geodesic loss function that improved performance.

work.name: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
work.position: Research Assistant & Undergraduate Thesis, advised by Prof. Yincong Chen
work.summary: Enhancing segmentation from datasets containing noisy labels using generative models.
highlights: Conducted research on applying noisy label segmentation to diffusion models for image generation tasks.
Proposed a novel approach for learning from noise-infused labels in both unsupervised and semi-supervised settings.
Utilized unlabeled and noisy-labeled image datasets to improve segmentation performance using Stable Diffusion.

work.name: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
work.position: Research Assistant, advised by Prof. Wu Yuan
work.summary: Multiplicative speckle noise denoising of OCT medical images based on Diffusion Models.
highlights: Developed a DDPM-based denoising method for speckle noise in OCT medical images to improve diagnostic accuracy.
Implemented noise modeling and diffusion training pipelines, and enhanced convergence speed and prediction efficiency.
Reproduced baseline models including DnCNN, U-Net, BM3D, TCFL-OCT, and DDPM for comparative evaluation.
Wrote Python scripts to compute denoising metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and GCMSE.

work.name: CVPR 2023 BDD100K Challenges
work.summary: Multi-object tracking to guide autonomous driving through machine learning algorithms.
highlights: Implemented object detection with advanced state-of-the-art detectors including YOLO and DINO.
Developed a multi-object tracking pipeline for autonomous driving using state-of-the-art machine learning models.
Ranked in the top 20% for Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) and achieved 1st place in Object Detection (OD) tasks.

work.name: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
work.position: Undergraduate Research Assistant, advised by Prof. Xiang Bai
work.summary: Recognition and extraction of musical notes using Optical Character Recognition (OCR).
highlights: Conducted research on text detection of musical notation using OCR techniques.
Built and annotated a specialized dataset from online musical tune data for model training and evaluation.
Evaluated models including DBNet, DBNet++, and PANet using the MMOCR framework and detection libraries.

education.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

projects.name: eSports Gaze Behavior Detection
projects.summary: Personalized eSports assistant using deep learning for gaze tracking across video frames (CNN, DETR, few-shot learning).
highlights: Built a cross-frame gaze estimation model using CNNs and temporal feature alignment.
Proposed a novel few-shot learning framework allowing rapid adaptation to users with minimal calibration data.
Final system supports real-time inference with <50ms latency on standard GPUs.

projects.name: Health Management System with Health Code and Trip Card
projects.summary: Health code system with QR code generation, data management, and epidemic risk level updates (SQL, C++, data structures).
highlights: Designed a structured user database supporting registration, trip tracking, and automated status updates.
Implemented modular features such as location-based risk evaluation and dynamic color coding.
